content: Cypress refers to a group of plants within the family Cupressaceae, which are coniferous species predominantly found in the temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere. The majority of cypress species are trees, although some are classified as shrubs. Most plants commonly referred to as cypress belong to the genera Cupressus and Chamaecyparis, though other genera within the Cupressaceae family also include species bearing the name cypress. The species Cupressus sempervirens is particularly notable for its exceptional longevity and has been cultivated as a popular ornamental plant for thousands of years. The term cypress originates from the Old French word cipres, which was derived from the Latin cyparissus, itself a Latinized form of the Greek word κῠπᾰ́ρῐσσος (kyparissos). Several species are commonly referred to as cypress, including: African Cypress (Widdringtonia species) Bald Cypress, Pond Cypress, and Montezuma Cypress (Taxodium species, native to North America) Chinese Swamp Cypress (Glyptostrobus pensilis) Cordilleran Cypress (Austrocedrus chilensis) Cypress (Callitropsis species) Cypress (Cupressus species) Cypress-pines (Actinostrobus species) Cypress-pines (Callitris species) False Cypress (Chamaecyparis species) Fujian Cypress (Fokienia hodginsii) Guaitecas Cypress (Pilgerodendron uviferum) Patagonian Cypress (Fitzroya cupressoides) Sargent Cypress (Cupressus sargentii) Siberian Cypress (Microbiota decussata) The Cupressaceae family also includes 13 to 16 additional genera that do not currently have cypress in their common names. The term cypress is also applied to an angiosperm vine within the bindweed family (Convolvulaceae), specifically the Cypress Vine (Ipomoea quamoclit). Additionally, the plant known as summer cypress refers to Bassia scoparia, which belongs to the family Amaranthaceae.
